# Tobit Chapter 7 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, Tobit 7 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/TOB_007_page_001.jpg

---

**7:1** And they-came to-Ecbatana and arrived at-the-house of-Raguel. And Sarah met them, and she-greeted them and they-greeted her back. And she-brought-them into the-house.

**7:2** And Raguel said to-Edna his-wife, "How-very-much the-young-man resembles Tobit my-kinsman!"

**7:3** And Raguel questioned them, "From-where are-you, brothers?"

And they-said to-him, "We [are] from the-sons of-Naphtali, those-captive in-Nineveh."

**7:4** And he-said to-them, "Do-you-know Tobit our-brother?"

And they-said, "We-know [him]."

And he-said, "Is-he well?"

**7:5** And they-said, "He-is alive and well."

And Tobias said, "He [is] my-father."

**7:6** And Raguel leaped-up and kissed him and wept. And he-blessed him and said to-him, "You-are the-son of-a-noble and good father. How-wretched it-is that a-righteous and merciful man has-become-blind!"

And he-embraced Tobias his-kinsman and wept.

**7:7** And Edna his-wife wept over-him, and Sarah their-daughter also wept.

**7:8** And Raguel slaughtered a-ram from-the-flock and they-received them warmly.

When they-had-washed and bathed and reclined-at-table to-eat, Tobias said to-Raphael, "Brother Azariah, speak to-Raguel that-he-may-give-me Sarah my-kinswoman."

**7:9** And Raguel heard [it] and said to-the-young-man, "Eat and drink, and be-merry this-night, for there-is no-one except you, brother, [who has the-right] to-take my-daughter Sarah — and indeed I myself am-not-free to-give her to-any-other-man, since you-are her-nearest-kinsman. But I-will-tell you the-truth, child:

**7:10** I-have-given her to-seven men of-our-brethren, and all-of-them died on-the-night when they-were-going-in to-her. But now, child, eat and drink, and the-Lord will-act on-your-behalf."

And Tobias said, "I-will-not eat or drink anything from-here, until you-establish my-claim and make-a-decision for-me."

And Raguel said, "Take [her] right-here and now; according-to the-decree of-the-book of-Moses she-is-given to-you — it-has-been-decreed from-heaven that she-be-given to-you. Take-her your-kinswoman, from-now-on you-are her-brother, and she-is your-sister. She-has-been-given to-you from-today and forever. The-Lord-of-heaven will-prosper you this-night, child, and will-grant you mercy and peace."

**7:11** And Raguel called Sarah his-daughter, and she-came to-him. And he-took-her by-the-hand and gave-her to-Tobias and said, "Take [her] according-to the-law and according-to the-decree written in-the-book of-Moses, that-she-be-your-wife. Take-her and bring-her safely to-your-father. And the-God of-heaven may-prosper your-way with-peace."

**7:12** And he-called Edna her-mother and he-took a-scroll and wrote a-marriage-contract and they-sealed [it].

**7:13** And then they-began to-eat.

**7:14** And Raguel called Edna his-wife and said to-her, "Sister, prepare the-other-room and lead her there."

**7:15** And she-went and made the-bed in-the room as-he-had-said to-her; and she-led Sarah there and wept over-her. And she-wiped-away her-tears and said to-her,

**7:16** "Take-heart, child; the-Lord of-heaven grant you joy instead-of your-grief. Take-heart, daughter."

And she-left.

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

- **7:2**: "How-very-much the-young-man resembles Tobit" — the resemblance triggers Raguel's emotional recognition. The Greek *poiōs homoioi* (how alike!) is literally rendered. The physical likeness is theologically significant: Tobias is the visible continuation of Tobit.
- **7:6**: "leaped-up and kissed him" — Greek *anepēdēsen* (sprang up). The physical energy of the greeting is preserved. The three-fold weeping (Raguel, Edna, Sarah at vv. 6–7) mirrors the threefold structure of hospitality.
- **7:8**: "slaughtered a-ram from-the-flock" — the word *krios* (ram) is specific. This is a full hospitality slaughter, not a domestic meal.
- **7:9**: "I-am-not-free to-give her to-any-other-man" — Greek *ou dunasthai* in the legal sense. The levirate restriction makes Raguel legally incapable of refusing Tobias.
- **7:10**: "Take [her] right-here and now" — Greek *labe autēn artion* — the colloquial immediacy of Raguel's capitulation is preserved. "Your-brother... your-sister" is a marriage convention term, not biological kinship. "From-today and forever" — a marriage formula.
- **7:11**: "according-to the-decree written in-the-book of-Moses" — second explicit citation of Mosaic law in two chapters.
- **7:12**: *bibliou* = scroll; *syngraphon* = written contract/document. The marriage contract (ketubbah-equivalent) is formalized in writing and sealed.
- **7:16**: "joy instead-of your-grief" — the Greek *charan anti tēs lypēs* is a formulaic blessing of reversal. Compare Ps 30:11 (LXX 29:12). — EMET
